sinusoidal-modeling-ferris.alt: Left: a Ferris wheel on a support above the ground, turning counterclockwise, with a seat S at the lowest point of the wheel, which is above the ground. Right: an unscaled graph of h(t), the height of the seat above the ground, for one turn. The graph starts at its lowest point F, rises through G to its highest point J, falls through K and ends at the lowest point M. G and K are at the height of the center of the wheel. The axes have no scale.

sinusoidal-modeling-tide.alt: An unscaled graph of W(t), the depth of water at a dock, for t from 2 to 14 hours after midnight. The graph starts at a high point P, falls through Q to a low point R, rises through S and ends at the next high point T. Q and S are halfway between the high and low depths. The axes have no scale.

sinusoidal-modeling-spring.alt: Left: a weight hanging from a spring attached to a beam, above a floor, bobbing up and down. Right: an unscaled graph of h(t), the height of the bottom of the weight above the floor, for one cycle. The graph starts at its highest point F, falls through G to its lowest point J, rises through K and ends at the highest point M. G and K are halfway between the highest and lowest heights. The axes have no scale.

sinusoidal-modeling-greenhouse.alt: An unscaled graph of T(t), the temperature in a greenhouse, in degrees Celsius, t hours after midnight, for t from 4 to 28. The graph starts at a lowest point P, rises through Q to a highest point R, falls through S and ends at the next lowest point U. Q and S are halfway between the lowest and highest temperatures. The axes have no scale.
